newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LONG AUSTRALIAN DEBT GET SQUEEZED AHEAD OF US DATA.
newsitem.headline: LONG AUSTRALIAN DEBT GET SQUEEZED AHEAD OF US DATA.

text.p: *Long Australian bond futures recovered almost all their early fall as late short-covering squeezed the market higher on the feeling that recent negativity had been overdone.
*U.S. retail sales to prove key test for debt markets.
Long Australian bond futures recovered almost all their early fall as a late bout of short-covering squeezed the market higher on the feeling that recent negativity had been over done.

The short-end of the curve remained in positive territory for most of the day following comments by Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane on Tuesday, which were seen leaving the door ajar for another easing in monetary policy.
"The weakness of the long-end had surprised a lot of people given that there was nothing negative in Macfarlane's speech and I think we saw that corrected this afternoon," one trader said.
The trader stressed that trade had largely been generated by the futures market and that physical flows had remained relatively thin.

Macfarlane said the RBA did not have a growth ceiling and that the economy could grow 4.5 percent or more over the next few years without sparking inflation. He also did not see monetary policy placing any constraint on growth.

The September and December bill futures contracts continued to trade at a discount to current official 5.0 percent interest rates, but are a long way from indicating a sixth rate cut in the current business cycle at this stage.
Westpac's consumer sentiment index for August rose just 0.2 percent, helping the market's late recovery.

Bill Evans, Westpac's General Manager, Economics, said the result was a very disappointing response given the last rate cut in July occurred about a week before the survey and indicated long term trends concerns with unemployment and the economy.
"Westpac believes that the Reserve Bank will move to reduce interest rates one more time sometime over the next few months, even though there may be some early signs of a stronger economy," he added.
However, the immediate focus is on the July U.S. retail sales report later on Wednesday and the U.S. Treasury market's reaction to it.

The U.S. is expecting the worst from the data, which is overshadowing other key data on CPI, PPI and industrial production this week, and has been largely in decline since the strong employment and NAPM index at the beginning of the month.
This fall has recently hampered any chance of the local market putting in any sustainable rally.
Forecasts for the data centre on a 0.7 percent rise with forecasts ranging as high as 1.2 percent.

The yield curve steepened sharply as the short-end outperformed against longer maturities, and also outpaced the rest of the dollar bloc. The long-end also reversed an initial margin widening against as the U.S. weakened further in Tokyo trading.
